cards.text: Job, the man from the land of Uz (Job 1:1), has just finished speaking. Now Bildad the Shuhite, one of his friends (Job 2:11), replies. He opens BIG: dominion and awe belong to God, and He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.

cards.question: Bildad keeps going about God with two questions: 'Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?' What is Bildad saying about God?

answers.text: He watches over only a few
He needs help to rule heaven

cards.question: Then Bildad turns from God to people. What does Bildad ask about people?

answers.text: Whether anyone can be right before God
Whether anyone can hide from God
Whether anyone can see God's face

cards.text: Then Bildad points to the night sky: if even the moon does not shine and the stars are not pure in His sight... Friend, I scrape one smudge off a cookie and call it perfect, and Bildad says the STARS don't pass inspection.

cards.question: True or false: Bildad says that compared to the moon and the stars, man looks more pure in God's sight.

cards.text: Bildad says how much less man, who is 'but a maggot,' and the son of man, who is 'but a worm!' Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and not ONE of the dead batteries I shared it with ever called me a maggot.
And just like that, Bildad is done. Then Job answers, and he opens with what sounds like a big compliment.

cards.question: Speaking to the one he's answering, Job says that person has saved the arm that is feeble and helped the ___.

cards.text: Then Job says, 'How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!' I bet that's the same voice you use when a coworker 'fixes' the printer by unplugging it and walking off: 'WOW. SO helpful. Thank you SO much.'

cards.question: Job asks the one who just spoke, 'To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?' What is Job questioning?

answers.text: When those words were first written
How long those words will go on

cards.text: Now Job talks about God's power, and he starts at the VERY bottom: the dead tremble, those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them. Most folks start a tour at the front door, friend, and Job starts his in the BASEMENT.

cards.question: Job talks about Sheol and Abaddon and how they look before God. What does he say about Sheol?

answers.text: It is too deep for Him

cards.text: Then Job looks up: God stretches out the north over empty space. Friend, I can't stretch out one sheet of cookie dough without it tearing in the middle.

cards.question: Job says God hangs the earth upon ___.

cards.text: NOTHING! I can't hang my apron on a hook without it hitting the floor, and He hangs the whole EARTH on nothing. Then Job points up at the clouds, where God wraps up the waters.

cards.question: True or false: Job says the clouds God wraps the waters in burst under their own weight.

cards.text: Job brings up the moon too: God covers the face of the full moon, spreading His cloud over it. Two speeches in a row, friend, and that poor moon can NOT catch a break.

cards.question: Job says God has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness. What does that picture show God doing?

answers.text: Marking a limit in His creation

cards.question: Job opened his tour of God's power by saying the dead tremble. Now he gets to the foundations of heaven. True or false: Job says the foundations of heaven quake at God's rebuke.

cards.text: The foundations of heaven QUAKE, astounded at His rebuke, and I jump when my oven timer beeps. Then Job says, 'By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.'

cards.question: Job adds that by His breath the skies were cleared, and His hand pierced the fleeing serpent. What do all the things Job lists here have in common?
After everything Job just listed about God's power, how much does Job say all of it shows of God's ways?

cards.text: Then Job says, 'How faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?' All of THAT was just the whisper, friend, and trust me, this story isn't over.
